statement.excerpt: As I wrote in the Subprime AI Crisis in September, in the event that these companies start charging what they actually need to, I hypothesize it will multiply the costs of their customers to the point that they can't afford to run their businesses — or, at the very least, will have to remove or scale back generative AI functionality in their products.

our_interpretation: The antecedent is a move by OpenAI or Anthropic to materially higher prices sufficient to cover the relevant provider costs.
A newly introduced premium model, higher token consumption, or a downstream company's own pricing change does not by itself establish that antecedent.
The outcome requires financial harm or feature reductions among affected business customers caused by the qualifying provider repricing.
The wording does not specify the affected share of customers, a cost multiplier, or a deadline.
criteria.support_condition: A documented cost-covering provider price increase multiplies affected customers' API expenditure and causes business failures or material reductions in their generative AI features.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After a documented qualifying repricing, representative affected customers absorb the costs and maintain their businesses and AI functionality, with evidence sufficient to reject the claimed customer consequence.
